name: Explora El Chalten

location.city: El Chalten (Los Huemules Conservation Reserve, Patagonia)

positioning: All-inclusive Patagonian wilderness lodge, officially Explora El Chaltén, set in the private Los Huemules Conservation Reserve on the Electrico River beneath the Marconi Glacier, bordering Los Glaciares National Park, with more than 30 guided Explorations included in the stay
best_for: Active travelers who want guided hikes, climbs and high-mountain ascents included in the stay
Hikers who want trails that start at the lodge door inside a private conservation reserve

facts.text: The lodge is wrapped in lenga and nirre forests.
The lodge is a base for exploring the Southern Patagonian Ice Field.
The lodge was designed by architect Pepe Jose Cruz.
The lodge's modern, minimalist architecture incorporates local materials and calming earth tones.
Explora El Chalten is the Chilean brand's first hotel in Argentina.
Rooms are designed to provide silence, privacy and space.
Bath products are crafted with the citrusy Patagonian herb paramela.
More than 30 guided Explorations are included with the stay.
Explorations are designed for small groups of no more than eight guests.
Each evening an Explora guide meets with guests to tailor the next day's Explorations to their preferences.
Open-fire cooking takes center stage, with fire-roasted beef and lamb and vegetables and tubers roasted in a traditional mud oven.
The stay includes breakfast, lunch and dinner, all beverages, regional wines and an open bar serving craft cocktails.

highlights.text: The lodge sits in the 14,000-acre Los Huemules Conservation Reserve and borders Los Glaciares National Park.
The lodge is set on the banks of the Electrico River under the Marconi Glacier.
The spa has five open-air hot tubs, two indoor saunas, a relaxation lounge, an outdoor sitting area and a shower with views of the valley.
The hotel was trucked down to Patagonia in 117 pieces and assembled on stilts to reduce its environmental impact.
Adventures include hikes to blue lagoons, rock climbing for beginners and experts, birding treks and high-mountain ascents with views to Mount Fitz Roy.

considerations.text: Because of the remote location, Wi-Fi in rooms and common areas may vary in reliability.
Wind gusts can reach hurricane strength, making some of the longer and higher-altitude hikes impossible.
Lunch service is not included on check-out day.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Explora El Chaltén
